Subject: Dev pilot: SDK developer runbook + local smoke tests

Hi Jason — thanks again for the demo call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned:

What we agreed: 
- Goal: validate a small local POC that demonstrates retrieval-augmented QA + a reranker and a structured-tool call for row lookups. Success = <200ms median token latency on local machine for short prompts, embeddings similarity top-3 relevant docs, reranker improves top-1 by at least 10pp on your eval set.
- Scope: two sample apps (Python FAQ agent and TypeScript KB-ranker demo) running on a developer laptop / CI smoke test.

Immediate next steps (short):
1) We’ll send a short developer runbook (attached: redwood_local_starter.md) with step-by-step SDK install and a local smoke-test checklist.
2) You’ll confirm which dataset we should seed (small KB dump vs. full index) — Jason, you mentioned 10–50 docs for first run.
3) We’ll provide both API-key-based quickstart for the POC and a note on OIDC/KMS options for later.

Infra & auth notes:
- For POC use: REDWOOD_API_KEY in env is simplest (we’ll provide a scoped key).
- For longer pilots: we recommend OIDC + per-service service accounts and KMS for keys.
- Routing: use per-request model_hint and region to prefer cheaper variants in us-east for bulk rerank jobs, and fall back to high-accuracy model in us-west for interactive paths.

SDKs and features we’ll exercise:
- Python and TypeScript SDKs (local runner + token streaming)
- Structured output and tool-calling (one example: get_row_from_db tool)
- Embeddings index + fast similarity + reranker pass
Attachments: redwood_local_starter.md (runbook), kb-ranker-sample.zip (small sample repo)

I’ll follow up with concrete commands and a tiny smoke-test script by EOD. Happy to hop on a short 20m next week if you want us to pair on the first run.

Thanks,
Monica Patel

Perfect — Python-first is fine. Below are the exact quickstart steps we recommend for a laptop-based smoke test. Paste into a terminal and you should have a working sample within ~10 minutes.

Python quickstart (venv recommended):
1) python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
2) pip install --upgrade pip
3) pip install redwood-inference-sdk==0.9.1
4) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
5) git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-kb-ranker.git && cd sample-kb-ranker/python_faq
6) python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
7) python smoke_test.py --seed-data ../sample_docs/20_docs.json

What smoke_test.py does (summary):
- calls /v1/embeddings to index the seed docs (local in-memory index for POC)
- runs a client-side similarity query (cosine) and prints top-3 results + similarity scores
- runs a single reranker_pass against the top-5 and prints reranked ordering and score delta
- runs a structured tool call example (get_row_from_db) that demonstrates tool-calling via the SDK and returns a JSON-structured response.

Notes:
- For POC you don’t need Redis; the SDK has an in-memory cache option. We’ll include a flag --use-redis in the runbook if you want to flip to Redis later.
- Node: TS sample requires Node >= 16.13; 18.x is fine. NPM install for TS sample (from repo root): npm install && cd ts_kb && npm run start:smoke

TypeScript quick check (one-liner example):
- npm i @redwood/inference && node -e "(async ()=>{const r=require('@redwood/inference');const c=new r.Client({apiKey:process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY});console.log(await c.embeddings.create({input:'test'}));})()"

Security:
- We’ll provision a scoped test API key limited to embeddings+generation for the demo. For production pilots we’ll recommend OIDC + short-lived tokens.

Links:
- Sample repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-kb-ranker
- Runbook (attached) contains exact env vars and troubleshooting steps.

If you want, we can provide a small Docker-compose with Redis + service to replicate the local run in CI.

Thanks — I’ll also ping Marissa to package the sample zip for you.

—Monica
